title: Bonus: 20 animation styles and the all-in-one prompt
book_insight: This is the prompt to keep coming back to. Pick a style from the list of 20, write your idea in one line, and choose your voice — your own recording or an ElevenLabs voice. One paste gives you a finished Reel. Rotating styles keeps your feed fresh: use one style for three videos, then switch.
book_reference: Steal Like an Artist — Austin Kleon
instructions: Pick a style from the list below, or combine two for something nobody else is posting.
Write your idea in one line — one idea per video.
Choose your voiceover. Your own voice: record it on your phone in a quiet room and save it in raw/ (MP3, WAV or M4A). An AI voice: let Claude write the script and make it with ElevenLabs.
Copy the all-in-one prompt, replace everything in [brackets], and delete the voiceover option you're not using.
Read the plan Claude shows you, ask for changes, then say “go ahead and render”.
Watch it on your phone and run the export checklist before posting.
Keep a note of which styles get the most shares and saves, and use those more often.

resources.label: 20 animation styles
resources.content:
Pick one — or combine two for something new (e.g. "Neon glow + Newspaper collage").

1. Kinetic typography — Big bold words animate in time with the voice. Fast cuts, punchy scale-ins, one or two accent colours.
2. Paper cut-out — Layered paper shapes with soft drop shadows and a slight stop-motion jitter. Warm, handmade feel.
3. Whiteboard doodle — Black marker lines draw themselves on a white board; a hand-drawn arrow or circle highlights each point.
4. Chalkboard — Chalk-textured lines and text on a dark board, revealed with dusty strokes. Great for lessons and tips.
5. Flat 2D motion graphics — Clean vector shapes, bright flat colours, smooth easing and icons that pop in.
6. Isometric 3D — Tiny isometric scenes and blocks that build themselves up piece by piece.
7. Neon glow — Glowing neon lines and text on a dark background, with a subtle flicker and light bloom.
8. Retro 80s synthwave — Sunset gradients, a glowing grid horizon, scanlines and chrome text.
9. Newspaper collage — Cut-out headlines, halftone photos, torn paper edges and tape, shuffled across the screen.
10. Glitch — RGB split, digital distortion and glitchy cuts between scenes. Edgy and fast.
11. Minimal line art — One continuous line that morphs from object to object on a plain background.
12. Claymation look — Soft, rounded 3D shapes with squishy, bouncy movement and a playful feel.
13. Pixel art — Chunky 8-bit sprites, game-style text boxes and retro sound cues.
14. Data story — Animated charts, counters ticking up and icons that make numbers feel dramatic.
15. Comic book — Panels, halftone dots, speech bubbles and big impact words like WOW or BAM.
16. Watercolour — Soft painted textures that bleed in, gentle fades and a calm, artistic mood.
17. Blueprint — White technical lines on a blue grid, with measurements and labels drawing in.
18. Liquid shapes — Gradient blobs that flow and morph into each new scene. Smooth and modern.
19. Split-screen before/after — The screen splits in two to compare wrong vs right, before vs after, or myth vs fact.
20. Notebook sketch — Lined paper, pen scribbles, sticky notes and highlighter swipes, like a study notebook.

resources.label: All-in-one video prompt
resources.content:
Make a vertical Instagram Reel (1080x1920, 30 fps) following CLAUDE.md.

ANIMATION STYLE: [STYLE — e.g. "Paper cut-out", or combine two: "Neon glow + Newspaper collage"]
IDEA: [YOUR IDEA IN ONE LINE — e.g. "3 money habits from The Psychology of Money"]
LENGTH: [20–30 seconds]

VOICEOVER — keep ONE option and delete the other:
A) Use my recording: raw/[your-voiceover-file.mp3]. Transcribe it (npx hyperframes transcribe or whisper), time every scene and caption to my words, and don't change what I say.
B) Generate it: write a voiceover script for the idea and show it to me. After I approve it, create the voice with the ElevenLabs API. Read the key from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and never print it. First tell me roughly how many characters it will use and suggest 3 voices that fit.

Then:
1. Show me the plan first: the hook (first 2 seconds), each scene with its on-screen text and length, and how the style will look (colours, fonts, motion). Wait for my OK.
2. Build it in studio-hyperframes (or studio-remotion if that suits the style better). Match the animation style closely, but never copy a reference video.
3. Add burned-in captions synced to the voice, plus quiet royalty-free background music and sound effects from free sources — log every file and its licence in credits.md. ElevenLabs is for the voice only.
4. Render to exports/[YYYY-MM-DD-short-title].mp4, check it against the export checklist, and tell me the file name and length.

resources.label: Recording your own voice
resources.content: Use your phone's voice recorder in a quiet room with soft furnishings, hold the phone about a hand's width from your mouth, and leave a second of silence at the start and end. Name the file clearly, e.g. raw/voiceover-money-habits.m4a.
